Sample. No seller, card, date, count or price on this page is real. Row heights are estimates from the code, not measurements.

Card in Hand: the eight parts the build does not draw

iPhone Duo, open pose, 951 x 669 pt, fold 40 pt at 455.5 pt. The keys panel draws from y 405 pt. Status bar foot drawn at 20 pt (unmeasured). Light theme only. Each part shows today's build, then the part as it should be built, inside today's layout. Debt duo-hand-mockup-gaps; decision duo-card-in-hand; the October mockup is docs/design/duo-card-in-hand/index.html at commit b8d11e7 (Duo round 2 draws Lost and degen's stack order as options).

Folded 1 Typed line mark 2 This envelope 3 Still owed here 4 Keep held 5 Held lines 6 Post at a tie 7 End of mail day 8 Suspense ranking All

1 · The typed card's line option picked: accent bar

The October mockup marks the typed card's line with a green fill (its .line.now, index.html:101 and :163). In the build, that fill is already the done fill (PackageCard.token(.rowFill) gives greenSoft for a done line). So the October mark does not carry over as drawn. Two options.

2 · This envelope, with its cards so far carried over

Carried over from October poses 1 to 3 (index.html:153, :223, :256): under "This envelope", the cards checked in since the last New envelope, or "Nothing checked in yet". Kept to one line, so the row stays the 44 pt that New envelope's hit frame already sets, and the button never moves.

3 · Still owed here option picked: on the order line

The figure is the package's own "N left · $Y" (decision outstanding-value-per-level; the bundle's packagePill, which PackagesModel.pills already holds). October drew it under the lines with card names (index.html:167). With the build's keys spanning both pages from y 405, a line under three or more lines sits under the keys. So the place is drawn as two options.

4 · Keep held carried over

Carried over from October pose 2 (index.html:271 to :272): the offer carries Keep held beside Post. It goes in today's offer slot under the sender (decision duo-card-in-hand, the Post offer paragraph; item 42 still open). A press on Keep held leaves a receipt of the same height, as Post does.

5 · Held cards marked on their lines carried over

Carried over from October pose 2 (index.html:102, :267 to :268): a line whose card waits on the Suspense line gets a manila tint, and its detail ends "on the Suspense line". The tint and the words are added from HandScreen, so ItemLine, which Packages and Tally share, does not change.

6 · Post here at a tie carried over

Carried over from October pose 2 (index.html:228 to :243): each envelope of a tie lists its lines and has its own Post button. A tie still has no first choice: the buttons weigh the same, and nothing posts until you press one (orphaned-mail-never-decides). The button reads "Post N cards here", the act's name on the offer, not October's bare "Post here".

7 · The end of mail day carried over; what opens it: option picked, the empty query

Carried over from October pose 5 (index.html:171 to :195, :382 to :406): the left page lists today's envelopes, and the right page names only what is not normal. What opens it October does not say, since there the query was simply empty. Two options. The past-14-days box is today's transitBox, unchanged.

8 · Suspense ranks the accounts it fits carried over

Carried over from October pose 3 (index.html:286 to :312): an envelope with no sender, whose cards are each in two envelopes. Its cards wait on the Suspense line, and the right page ranks the accounts they fit by named copies. Post checks in the named cards only. The rank is the bundle's rankCandidates, the rule Orphaned already uses. When the top two rank equal, the page shows the tie of part 6 instead.

Sizes and sources

  • Screen: folded Duo, 466 pt wide (duo-fold-and-keyboard, outer screen, re-measured 2026-11-08). Open Duo right page: 455.5 pt (same record). layout.py devices gives unknown for this repo.
  • Gutters: the list pads 16 pt (OrphanedView.list); the candidates block pads 8, 12, 12 (EnvelopeCard.card); a row pads 8 with an 8 pt gap to "This one" (CandidateRow.body). So the text column at the default size is 394 pt less "This one".
  • Type, at the default size: seller Cochin 14 bold, relative to Body; meta Menlo 10.5, relative to Caption 1; fit line Menlo 11, Caption 1; "This one" Menlo 11.5, Caption 1 (CandidateRow.body, MiniLabel). Header micro Menlo 11, entries Cochin 13.5 Body, tie line Cochin 12.5 Footnote (EnvelopeCard.card).
  • Scaling: Font.custom(_:size:relativeTo:) scales each size by its text style. Ratios from Apple's iOS Dynamic Type tables (typography page, read 2026-11-08, 200): Body 17, 23, 40, 53; Caption 1 12, 18, 32, 43; Footnote 13, 19, 33, 44, at Large (default), xxxLarge, AX3 and AX5. So the meta line draws at 10.5, 15.75, 28 and 37.6 pt.
  • Colours: candidate meta and fit line inkSoft, seller ink, row border line, tie line manilaInk on manila (OrphanedPaint.token, ControlPaint).
  • The audit's text size on 2026-10-27: unmeasured. OrphanedUITests.launch passes no -UIPreferredContentSizeCategoryName, so the tie audit ran at the simulator's own setting, which no record names. AX5 is drawn as the worst case; it is the size DuoSpreadUITests.testFlatBarLabelsFitThePillAtAccessibilityXXXL uses.
  • Width of "This one" at AX3 and AX5: unmeasured. Drawn at its natural width, capped at half the row, so it wraps to two lines there.
  • Line heights: Chromium's, not SwiftUI's. Row heights are estimates within a few points.

Sample data. The ledger in every frame is the test fixture shared/fixtures/ledger.json (12 lines, 4 packages, $67.50), so its counts and dollar figures are not real. The frames are headless Chromium screenshots of the built index.html, and the px readings under them were measured on those pages.

Panel paper fill

Waiting item 63, panel-paper-fill. Should an overlay panel on the Ledger tab paint the paper colour, so the rows under it stop showing through? Every frame but the last draws the overlay the owner ruled on 2026-10-11 (motion-disclosure-panels-arrive). The owner ruled that panels overlay the list, not where they sit. The overlay is not built yet, so a style override draws it here, and its geometry is a guess: the panel keeps its place, is as wide as its card, and runs past the card's foot over the rows below. Where a panel cuts a row below it, that cut comes from this guess. Only the panel's fill differs between the options.

Sizes and sources

  • Shots and readings come from shots/panel-paper-fill/capture.mjs; run it again to retake them.
  • Widths 375 and 760 px, height 812: WIDTHS and openSeeded in test/screens.mjs. Device scale 2.
  • One theme, light: shared/tokens.json holds one palette, and src/app.jsx has no dark rule.
  • Panel style: panelWrap in src/app.jsx (padding 4px 8px 12px, top rule line, no background). Callers: the Sorted by and Orders from panels in the View card, and the Sync, Recent and History panels in the Data card.
  • Paper: paper #F2E9DA. The Ledger cards are card #FCF6EA (.mdl-lcard), so a paper panel reads darker than the card it opens from.
  • The overlay is drawn by a style override, not built: the panel is absolute at its own place in flow, as wide as its card, over the rows. The card drops overflow: hidden so the panel can pass its foot. That geometry is this mockup's guess; motion-disclosure-panels-arrive gives no geometry.
  • Row tops are read from the page. They are the same in all three overlay frames at each width, so the fill and the rule move nothing (no-layout-shift-under-pointer).
  • Unmeasured: the Sync and Recent panels (no sync key and no recent taps in the fixture), the Orders from panel, and touch-device rendering.
